answer: Disjoint-path routing quota. Capacity is capped by distinct, non-overlapping neighbor groups reachable via edge-disjoint paths; a cluster attached through one inlet gains no extra quota. New counterparties must use paths that do not share an upstream bridge, so a glacier of cheap internal edges cannot inflate capacity. Each sybil thus needs independent attachment and sustained traffic through separate honest neighborhoods—an oasis of real topology paid per identity in extra links and routing load.
